To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the lack of performance-related reinforcement from leaders is a significant and important leadership phenomenon that is distinct from other leadership constructs, is associated with a variety of important outcomes, and has implications for leadership development and training.

(a) reward omission and punishment omissions are related to follower satisfaction, leader effectiveness, role clarity, and performance, and (b) reward omission and punish omission are related to each other, to leader consideration and structure, and to leader reward and punishment.

(1) the lack of response from the leader (omission) is a unique and important form of laissez-fare leadership, (2) omission is a distinct construct from the other forms of laissez-fair leadership, (3) omission is negatively related to follower satisfaction and perceived role clarity, and (4) omission is negatively (and in the case of punishment omission) significantly related to subordinate performance
In summary, our research is concerned with
the absence of leadership.
the effects of the absence of leadership.
a single aspect of laissez-fair leadership, namely, the failure to provide contingent reinforcement.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the leader who fails to reward good performance, and who fails to punish poor performance, is a leader who fails to lead.

the leader reward omission and the punishment omission have a strong negative relationship with the leader effectiveness, role clarity, subordinate performance and the follower satisfaction with the leaders.

this article has provided evidence that a lack of performance-contigent reinforcement is an important leadership behavior that is related to subordinate satisfaction with the leader and subordinate-rated leader effectiveness.

the absence of leadership is just as important as the presence of leadership.
leader non-reinforcement is a distinct form of laissez faire leadership that is related to subordinate satisfaction and performance.
